feature: Issue 193: preserve message order and attribution under concurrent operators

userStories.title: Registry mixed-sender characterization
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want the steering-registry tests to characterize mixed-sender FIFO, idempotent replay, and idle send_now behavior, so that the registry's actual concurrency contract is pinned before any route- or executor-level proof.
acceptanceCriteria: The existing msg() helper in packages/workflows/src/steering-registry.test.ts accepts an optional operatorUserId defaulting to 'user-1', leaving all current tests unchanged.

A new test named 'mixed senders keep order and attribution through drain' accepts a1, b1, a2, b2 on one handle with alternating op-a/op-b senders; asserts snapshot ids and senders in exact call order; asserts each sender's filtered subsequence is stable; drains once asserting the same objects/order; and asserts a second drain is empty.

The existing 'duplicate id with different prose keeps the original' test is strengthened so the original is from op-a and the replay from op-b, and the stored row still contains op-a plus the original prose (an id cannot reattribute a message).
The existing idle send_now test assigns queued messages to op-a and the releasing message to op-b, asserting the wake batch retains both senders in accepted order.
(cd packages/workflows && bun test src/steering-registry.test.ts src/node-transcript.test.ts) passes.

No timers, real database, server, or filesystem fixture is added; no redundant cross-run, withdraw, anonymous-sender, or same-identity/tab matrix is introduced; no production code is changed unless a focused assertion fails (then the fix is minimal and in a separate commit).
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase 1 (phase-01-registry-order-and-isolation.md). Modify ONLY packages/workflows/src/steering-registry.test.ts. Re-read steering-registry.ts: NodeSteeringHandle.accept() at ~line 290 pushes to this.pending (306) with first-wins send_now batch release (314-318); drain() at 359-363 returns and clears pending. node-transcript.test.ts already proves appendOperatorTranscript input order + per-row operator_user_id/message_id — do not duplicate. Conditional production owner only after a proven red: steering-registry.ts.

userStories.title: Deterministic route concurrency test
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want one Hono-route test that holds operator A at the identity-resolution seam while operator B completes, so that the accept()-order chosen by the server is proven to drive both the handle snapshot and the public queue read with per-request attribution.
acceptanceCriteria: In the existing queued-guidance describe of packages/server/src/routes/api.workflow-runs.test.ts, a test named 'overlapping identity streams preserve accept order and request attribution' is added.

A temporary identity mock keyed by header value blocks operator A inside findOrCreateUserByPlatformIdentity via a test-owned aEntered/releaseA promise pair; the default identity mock is restored in finally even if an assertion fails.

The test starts A1 and waits until A is held; sends B1 and awaits its 200; sends/awaits B2 from the same stream; releases A and awaits A1; then sends/awaits A2 — proving B's requests reached synchronous accept() while A had not.
The handle is asserted to contain [B1, B2, A1, A2] with senders [op-b, op-b, op-a, op-a], original text, no duplicate ids, and sender-filtered subsequences [B1, B2] and [A1, A2].
A GET of the queue returns the same id/text order with objects containing exactly message_id and message — no attribution fields.
Every send response is the existing 200 receipt shape.
(cd packages/server && bun test src/routes/api.workflow-runs.test.ts -t 'overlapping identity streams') passes, and the full api.workflow-runs.test.ts file passes.

No timers, microtask counts, or call-indexed getWorkflowRun gates are used; no registry prototype spying or test-only runtime imports; no route contract change; no copies of already-covered actor/anonymous/malformed/duplicate/terminal/scoping tests.
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase 2 (phase-02-route-concurrency-integration.md). Modify packages/server/src/routes/api.workflow-runs.test.ts only; conditional owner after proven failure is packages/server/src/routes/api.ts (POST nodes/:nodeId/send handler ~line 5343, handle.accept at 5426, identity via userDb.findOrCreateUserByPlatformIdentity; GET queue at 5650). Reuse postNodeSend, sendPayload, liveSetup; use valid distinct UUID message ids. Default mockFindOrCreateUserByPlatformIdentity returns the header value as the canonical test user id. This test owns deterministic server overlap — the E2E journey uses the queue snapshot as oracle instead.

userStories.title: Executor mixed-sender transcript chain
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want the existing direct, idle send_now, and loop executor delivery tests strengthened for mixed senders, so that every production drain path demonstrates the same receipt-order and per-message identity metadata.
acceptanceCriteria:
The existing 'drains queued guidance as one follow-up turn' test in packages/workflows/src/dag-executor.test.ts enqueues a1/op-a, b1/op-b, a2/op-a, b2/op-b in that receipt order; asserts resumed prompt order a1

b1

a2

b2; asserts operator rows ordered by seq carry the four matching ids/senders; asserts each sender's subsequence is stable; and asserts all four rows use the caused turn's attempt and precede its assistant row.

steeringMessage, enqueue, and sendNow helpers accept an optional operator id preserving the current default; the existing old-plus-new redirect (send_now) test assigns queued messages to op-a and the releasing message to op-b and asserts the three transcript senders in batch order alongside the current id/order/attempt assertions.
The existing loop-guidance delivery test enqueues one op-a and one op-b message and asserts prompt, ids, senders, seq, caused attempt, and identical loop ancestry for both.

(cd packages/workflows && bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts) passes and (cd packages/server && bun test src/routes/api.workflow-runs.test.ts) remains green (existing display-name A/B/A read-model coverage stays green).

No concurrent sibling-node tests are added here (registry key isolation is unit-tested; cross-node behavior is US-004); no new polling, timers, mock modules, or production abstractions; no executor change unless a path fails while others pass — then fix only the divergent drain/writer wiring in a separate commit.
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase 3 (phase-03-executor-transcript-chain.md). Modify packages/workflows/src/dag-executor.test.ts only. Reusable coverage: appendOperatorTranscript already writes one row per input item in array order with verbatim operator_user_id/message_id (node-transcript.test.ts); the #181 queued-guidance test already verifies a direct mixed op-a/op-b batch; api.workflow-runs.test.ts already has the A/B/A display-name read-model test — do not duplicate either. Conditional production owner after proven failure: packages/workflows/src/dag-executor.ts.

userStories.title: E2E two-operator journey on Legacy and Console
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want one Playwright scenario per shell where two identity contexts launch overlapping dock sends to a live node, so that the real server/registry/executor/DB/read-model/rendering chain proves queue order, transcript order, attribution, and sibling-node isolation end to end.
acceptanceCriteria: One parameterized test per existing surface loop is added to e2e/ui/agent-queue-convergence.spec.ts named '[P1] [V:steer.concurrent-operators-${surface}] overlapping operators keep queue, transcript, and attribution aligned on ${surface}'.

Starter and teammate contexts/pages use the existing 460x900 narrow viewport; the pair workflow starts and steer-a and steer-b emit node_started; steer-a opens in both identities' rooms with starter/non-starter verified via the existing run-detail seam.

Round 1 pre-fills distinct A1/B1 texts, registers both response listeners, and presses both docks' Queue shortcuts inside one Promise.all; round 2 repeats concurrently for A2/B2 only after both round-1 responses — preserving A1<A2 and B1<B2 while allowing either global interleaving.
One distinct teammate message X1 is sent to steer-b via the teammate request context with an explicit UUID as the cross-node control.

Both server queues are snapshotted immediately: steer-a contains exactly the four A/B ids with no duplicates, A1 before A2, B1 before B2 — saved as queueOrder without prescribing which sender won a round; steer-b contains exactly [X1].
Before drain, both steer-a rooms converge on queueOrder showing the four-row queue state (queued · 4, no duplicates, no cross-node text).

After the real workflow completes, steer-a transcript operator-row ids exactly equal queueOrder with increasing seq; A rows show display name e2e-starter with one stable non-null user id and starter texts; B rows show e2e-hitl-teammate with a different stable non-null user id and teammate texts; steer-b contains only X1 with the same teammate user id/name; no A/B id or text appears under the wrong node or sender.
Reopened completed steer-a room in both contexts shows DOM operator rows, operator · <name> labels, bodies, and sent badges following queueOrder exactly.

(cd e2e && npm run typecheck), (cd e2e && npx playwright test agent-queue-convergence --grep 'steer.concurrent-operators'), and the full agent-queue-convergence spec pass; neighboring convergence assertions (queue-band geometry, labels, Console-at-1440 page viewport) remain green.

No fixture, product file, or visual-design change; no arbitrary sleeps (queue snapshot is the order oracle; if drain beats the snapshot, reduce pre-send setup work first and only adjust the bounded 45s fixture delay with measured CI evidence).
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase 4 (phase-04-e2e-two-operator-journey.md). Extend e2e/ui/agent-queue-convergence.spec.ts — do not create a separate spec. It already owns starter/teammate browser contexts, Console and Legacy room navigation, the two-node e2e-queue-guidance-pair fixture, and queue GET/DOM-id/node-start/viewport/queue-visual helpers. Import listNodeMessages from e2e/lib/playwright/run-detail.ts. The fake provider's resumed turn completes without a new scenario block. Deterministic overlap is owned by US-002's route test; this journey proves the persisted chain against whichever order the registry chose. If a timing failure appears, run the new scenarios twice and remove the race source rather than widening timeouts.

userStories.title: Closeout: evidence report, test plan, tracker, gates
userStories.description: As an Archon maintainer, I want the Story 2.13 evidence recorded, the steering test plan mapped to the final tests, the tracker moved to done, and all repository gates green, so that issue #193 can close with reproducible proof.
acceptanceCriteria: In _bmad-output/specs/spec-agent-node-room/steering-test-plan.md the single generic concurrent-operators bullet is replaced by a concise mapping to the mixed-sender registry characterization, the deterministic overlapping Hono-route test, the strengthened direct/idle/loop executor tests, and the two [V:steer.concurrent-operators-*] scenarios.

The test plan states semantics precisely: global order is accept() order; within-sender order assumes one dock/request stream waits for its prior send response; the shared node queue means 'no cross-user leakage' is no sender substitution, not private visibility; queue GET intentionally omits attribution.

plans/260920-0444-issue-193-concurrent-operator-order-attribution/reports/characterization-evidence.md is created with commands, pass/fail summaries, scenario ids, and any production defect fixed (without duplicating implementation details that live in code/tests).

Only the 2-13-preserve-message-order-and-attribution-under-concurrent-operators entry in _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/agent-node-room/sprint-status.yaml changes to done, and only after every focused and full gate passes.

Narrow gates pass: (cd packages/workflows && bun test src/steering-registry.test.ts src/node-transcript.test.ts); (cd packages/server && bun test src/routes/api.workflow-runs.test.ts); (cd packages/workflows && bun test src/dag-executor.test.ts); (cd e2e && npm run typecheck); (cd e2e && npx playwright test agent-queue-convergence --grep 'steer.concurrent-operators').

Neighbor + repo gates pass: (cd e2e && npx playwright test agent-queue-convergence agent-queue-guidance) and bun run validate. bun.lock and e2e/package-lock.json are unchanged (any lock change is a setup error).
No evergreen product docs are changed; no migration, rollout, config, generated output, or background process is introduced.
userStories.technicalNotes: Phase 5 (phase-05-closeout-and-spec-sync.md). Validation order: bun install --frozen-lockfile and (cd e2e && npm ci && npx playwright install chromium) only if deps missing; narrow gates first, then neighboring E2E + bun run validate. bun run validate does NOT run the standalone Playwright project — both command sets are required; never substitute root bun test for the root gate. Final review checklist: observed queue order = persisted/displayed order; no lock/lane/timestamp-sort/widened wire contract; queue response stays two fields; transcript metadata stays origin/operator_user_id/message_id plus existing execution scope.
